messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call for high-severity incident affecting tenant AcmeCorp-VPC in dedicated pool dp-nyc-2. Alert: 65% generation error rate and increased latency for pinned model variant redwood-3b-quantized. Customers experiencing timeouts and degraded responses. Please ack and triage.

tai_oncall: Ack. I’m taking this. Starting triage — collecting recent deploys and model-version pins. ETA 20–30m.

sara_ops: Noted impact on AcmeCorp. I’ll open a customer channel and prep a short status to share. Can someone confirm whether any autoscale events happened around 02:10 UTC?

mohit_reliability: Looking at metrics now. There was a rolling quantized-kernel rollout to dp-nyc-2 at 01:58 UTC (batching/quantization kernel switch). Error spike lines up with that. Kernel telemetry shows elevated KV-cache eviction errors for sequence lengths >1024.

incident-bot: Attached logs: `/var/log/runtime/dp-nyc-2/2025-06-10/kv-cache-errors.log` (tail lines) and rollout job id `rollout-20250610-0158`.

kate_vpc_admin: Confirming tenant isolation: AcmeCorp-VPC is the only tenant pinned to redwood-3b-quantized on that pool; others use dynamic routing. If we need immediate mitigation we can apply a tenant-specific override to route Acme requests to a safe fallback model in another pool.

tai_oncall: Proposal: apply immediate customer override to pin Acme to `redwood-3b-safe-v2` (non-quantized) and roll back the kernel change on dp-nyc-2. Rolling both mitigations in parallel: 1) tenant override (fast), 2) kernel rollback (slower, requires infra window). Any objections?

mohit_reliability: +1 on both. Tenant override first. That avoids customer impact quickly while we validate rollback. We should also monitor cache pressure — the rollback will clear pathological state.

ellen_cs: I’ve messaged AcmeCorp in the support channel: "We’re investigating increased errors for your VPC. We’re applying a temporary routing override to a safe model variant; you should see normal responses within a few minutes. We’ll follow up with root cause and timeline." They replied: "Thanks — please keep us updated, it’s customer-facing."

eng-lead-jamie: Quick reminder: ensure the override does not remove any customer-specific model customizations (Acme has prompt templates and a pinned tokenizer config). Use `--preserve-config` flag.

incident-bot: TL;DR mitigation plan: 
- apply tenant override to route Acme requests to `redwood-3b-safe-v2` in pool dp-nyc-1 (no quantization)
- mark temporary pin `tenant_override=true` in control plane
- rollback quantization kernel in dp-nyc-2 via infra rollback job `rollback-20250610-kernel`
- monitor throughput/errors and update customer

tai_oncall: Executing tenant override command now:

```
# run from ops-console
redwood tenant-override set --tenant AcmeCorp-VPC --model redwood-3b-safe-v2 --pool dp-nyc-1 --preserve-config --note "incident mitigation 2025-06-10"
```

tai_oncall: Command returned success. Control plane reports active override and traffic draining from dp-nyc-2 to dp-nyc-1 for Acme.

sara_ops: I see traffic shift in metrics. Error rate for Acme down from 65% to 2% in ~90s. Latency stable. Sending update to customer.

ellen_cs: Sent update: "We applied a temporary routing override to a safe model variant; errors have dropped significantly. We will keep this in place while we complete rollback and verification. ETA for full rollback 2–3 hours." Acme replied :thumbsup:.

mohit_reliability: On the rollback side — kernel rollback job queued. I’ll coordinate with eng-infra for safe window to avoid broader disruptions. Kernel rollback will also trigger a small restart of runtime pods in dp-nyc-2; we plan a staggered restart to preserve capacity.

kate_vpc_admin: Note: Because Acme was single-tenant pinned on dp-nyc-2, once rollback completes we should remember to remove the temporary override and re-pin if customer prefers original variant. Will track that as an action item.

eng-lead-jamie: Action items summary (for postmortem traceability):
- tai_oncall: Tenant override applied at 2025-06-10T02:15:07Z (thread_ts + 260s).
- mohit_reliability: Kernel rollback job started at 2025-06-10T02:34:00Z.
- sara_ops / ellen_cs: Customer communications logged in support thread #ACME-523.
- kate_vpc_admin: Confirm and re-apply any customer-specific tokenizer/prompt pins after testing.

incident-bot: Handoff note: on-call coverage change in 30m — @mohit_reliability please take primary ownership for post-rollback verification and postmortem write-up after handoff.

mohit_reliability: Taking handoff. I’ll validate KV-cache metrics and run the synthetic prompt-set suite against Acme's workload while the override remains. If rollback verification passes, we can remove tenant override and re-pin to preferred model or suggest a safer quantized profile.

tai_oncall: Quick troubleshooting snippet that helped identify the issue (from runtime logs):

```
ERROR runtime.kvcache: failed to deserialize kv-entry seqlen=1208 key=cache:tok:abcd... err=checksum-mismatch
WARN runtime.attn-kernel: fallback to unoptimized path for seqlen>1024
```

mohit_reliability: That checksum-mismatch is the smoking gun. It looks like the quantized kernel's serialization format had an edge-case for long context windows. We’ll add a safety-check to the kernel that rejects persisted entries that don't match new checksum format rather than causing exceptions — longer-term fix.

eng-lead-jamie: Please put an immediate guard into the kernel rollout pipeline: block quantized-kernel rollouts against pools with >1 single-tenant pinned customer until we have checksum guards. Create an RFC/short doc and add to rollout gating.

mohit_reliability: Filed ticket INF-7823: "Kernel checksum guard + rollout gating for single-tenant pools" and linked rollout job ids.

kate_vpc_admin: Kernel rollback completed at 2025-06-10T04:00:00Z per infra logs. Staggered restarts finished.

mohit_reliability: Running synthetic tests now. All green against `redwood-3b-safe-v2`. KV-cache errors on dp-nyc-2 have returned to baseline. I recommend we keep tenant override for 1 hour to observe production traffic, then remove and re-evaluate.

ellen_cs: Updated Acme with final timeline and that we’ll confirm before switching them back. They asked for a one-paragraph RCA once ready.

tai_oncall: Marking incident as mitigated. Temporary override remains until 05:00 UTC for observation.

eng-lead-jamie: Good work. Please include the following in the postmortem: sequence of rollout jobs, why single-tenant pin increased blast radius, mitigation timing, and customer communication timeline. Assign owner for follow-through.

mohit_reliability: I’ll own the postmortem write-up (INF-7823 includes the postmortem subtask). Planning a 1hr blameless review tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated. Summary: tenant-level override applied (Acme -> redwood-3b-safe-v2), quantized kernel rollback on dp-nyc-2, monitoring shows error rate returned to baseline. Impact window ~01:58–02:15 UTC (customer errors), extended verification and rollback completed by 04:00 UTC.

sara_ops: Filing follow-up tasks: customer re-pin decision, update rollout gating, postmortem agenda.

ellen_cs: I’ll draft the one-paragraph RCA for Acme and coordinate review with Mohit & Jamie before sending.

tai_oncall: Handoff complete — signing off. If anything regresses, reopen this thread.

mohit_reliability: Taking runbook ownership. Will post links to logs, rollback jobs, and synthetic test results in the postmortem doc.

eng-lead-jamie: Thanks team. Please add any performance/cost notes about fallback model (dp-nyc-1) so Support can advise on potential billing/latency changes when customer is switched back.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging. React with :eyes: to acknowledge you’ve read the final mitigation summary."
